en: Can I sit next to you in the class?
tamil: நான் கிளாஸ்ல உன் பக்கத்துல உட்காரலாமா?
explain: 'Can I' asks for permission. 'Next to' means beside.
usage: Use it on your first day in a new class or college.
leelaQ: Where do you like to sit in a class?
answer: I like to sit in the middle so I can see and hear well.

en: My daughter goes to tuition after school.
tamil: என் பொண்ணு ஸ்கூல் முடிஞ்சு டியூஷனுக்கு போறா.
context: A parent chatting with another parent.
explain: 'Tuition' means private lessons in India. 'Goes' has -es because of 'she'.
usage: Use it with other parents when you talk about your child's routine.
leelaQ: Do children need tuition after school?
answer: Some do, but good teaching in school is enough for many.

en: I have understood this topic now, thank you.
tamil: எனக்கு இப்போ இந்த டாபிக் புரிஞ்சிடுச்சு, நன்றி.
context: Thanking a teacher after an explanation.
explain: 'Have understood' shows the result is clear now. 'Thank you' makes it polite.
usage: Use it with a teacher or friend after they explain a difficult point.
leelaQ: What was the last difficult thing you understood?
answer: I understood how bank interest is calculated.

en: Where can I get the previous year question papers?
tamil: முந்தைய வருஷ கேள்வித்தாள்கள் எங்க கிடைக்கும்?
explain: 'Where can I get' asks for a place or source. 'Previous year' means last year.
usage: Use it with seniors or the librarian before an exam.
leelaQ: Where do you usually find study material?
answer: I find it on the college website and in the library.

en: Writing the answers by hand helps me remember them.
tamil: விடைகளை கையால எழுதினா அது எனக்கு நினைவுல இருக்கும்.
explain: 'Writing' is a gerund used as the subject of the sentence.
usage: Use it when you discuss study methods with friends.
leelaQ: How do you remember new words?
answer: I write them in a notebook and use them in sentences.

en: I can't concentrate when the TV is on.
tamil: டிவி ஓடிட்டு இருக்கும்போது என்னால கவனம் செலுத்த முடியாது.
explain: 'Can't' shows inability. 'When' joins the problem with its cause.
usage: Use it at home when you need quiet for your studies.
leelaQ: What helps you concentrate on your work?
answer: A quiet room and a cup of tea help me.

en: Please give me a little more time to finish this.
tamil: இதை முடிக்க எனக்கு இன்னும் கொஞ்சம் நேரம் கொடுங்க.
context: Asking a teacher during a test.
explain: 'A little more' softens the request. 'To finish' gives the reason.
usage: Use it with a teacher or a lecturer when you are almost done.
leelaQ: What do you do when you need more time?
answer: I politely ask my manager for a short extension.

en: The seminar was very useful for all the students.
tamil: அந்த செமினார் எல்லா மாணவர்களுக்கும் ரொம்ப பயனுள்ளதா இருந்துச்சு.
explain: 'Was' links the seminar with the description. 'Useful for' shows who benefits.
usage: Use it in feedback forms or when you speak to a principal about an event.
leelaQ: Did you attend any useful programme recently?
answer: Yes, I attended a workshop on time management.

en: Have you prepared for the viva?
tamil: நீ வைவாவுக்கு தயாராகிட்டியா?
explain: 'Viva' is an oral exam. 'Have you prepared' checks the present state of readiness.
usage: Use it with lab partners before the oral exam.
leelaQ: Do you feel confident about speaking in an exam?
answer: I feel a little nervous, but I know my subject.

en: I am going to apply for a scholarship this year.
tamil: நான் இந்த வருஷம் ஒரு ஸ்காலர்ஷிப்புக்கு விண்ணப்பிக்கப் போறேன்.
context: Telling a friend about a plan.
explain: 'Am going to' shows a plan already decided.
usage: Use it with friends or teachers when you talk about funds for studies.
leelaQ: What are your plans for higher studies?
answer: I want to do a master's degree after my graduation.

en: Last week I attended a workshop on public speaking.
tamil: போன வாரம் நான் பொது பேச்சு பத்தின ஒரு வொர்க்ஷாப்புக்கு போனேன்.
explain: 'Last week' sets the time at the start. 'Attended' is used for events.
usage: Use it at the office or in class when you share a training experience.
leelaQ: Are you comfortable speaking in front of people?
answer: Not yet, but I am practising every day.

en: What time will the results be published?
tamil: ரிசல்ட் எத்தனை மணிக்கு வெளியிடுவாங்க?
context: Asking an office or a friend.
explain: 'Will be published' is passive future. 'What time' asks for the clock time.
usage: Use it on result day when you check with a friend or a clerk.
leelaQ: What will you do after you see your results?
answer: I will call my parents first.

en: You can learn almost anything from YouTube these days.
tamil: இப்போல்லாம் யூடியூப்ல இருந்து கிட்டத்தட்ட எல்லாத்தையும் கத்துக்கலாம்.
explain: 'Can' shows it is possible. 'Almost' means nearly.
usage: Use it when you encourage a friend who cannot afford coaching.
leelaQ: What did you learn from the internet recently?
answer: I learned how to make a simple website.

en: Could you recommend a good book for learning grammar?
tamil: இலக்கணம் கத்துக்க ஒரு நல்ல புத்தகத்தை பரிந்துரைக்க முடியுமா?
explain: 'Recommend' means suggest something good. 'Could you' is polite.
usage: Use it with an English teacher or a friend who studies well.
leelaQ: What book are you reading these days?
answer: I am reading a short story book in English.

en: The results will come out next Friday.
tamil: ரிசல்ட் அடுத்த வெள்ளிக்கிழமை வரும்.
explain: 'Come out' means to be published. 'Will' is used for a known future fact.
usage: Use it when a student or a parent asks when the marks will arrive.
leelaQ: How do you feel before the results come?
answer: I feel a little scared, but I hope for the best.

en: He will not join the tuition next year.
tamil: அவன் அடுத்த வருஷம் டியூஷன்ல சேர மாட்டான்.
context: Telling a neighbour about a decision.
explain: 'Will not' shows a decision or a refusal about the future.
usage: Use it when you talk about a student's decision with other parents.
leelaQ: Do you think tuition is necessary?
answer: Not always, because self-study can also work well.

en: Did you take notes in yesterday's class?
tamil: நேத்து கிளாஸ்ல நீ நோட்ஸ் எடுத்தியா?
explain: 'Yesterday's class' shows the class belongs to yesterday.
usage: Use it when you were absent and need to catch up.
leelaQ: How do you catch up when you miss a class?
answer: I take my friend's notes and read them at home.

en: He is good at maths but weak in English.
tamil: அவன் கணக்குல கெட்டிக்காரன், ஆனா இங்கிலீஷ்ல வீக்.
explain: 'Good at' and 'weak in' are fixed phrases. 'But' shows the contrast.
usage: Use it when you describe a student to a teacher or a parent.
leelaQ: What subject are you good at?
answer: I am good at science and history.

en: I have been studying since six in the morning.
tamil: நான் காலையில ஆறு மணியிலிருந்து படிச்சிட்டு இருக்கேன்.
context: Telling a friend why you are tired.
explain: 'Have been studying' with 'since' shows an action that started in the past and still continues.
usage: Use it when you explain your tiredness or ask for a break.
leelaQ: How long can you study without a break?
answer: I can study for about one hour without a break.

en: Which topic is the teacher going to cover next?
tamil: டீச்சர் அடுத்து எந்த டாபிக்கை எடுக்கப் போறாங்க?
context: Asking a classmate about the plan.
explain: 'Cover a topic' means to teach it. 'Going to' asks about a plan.
usage: Use it with classmates to read the next lesson in advance.
leelaQ: Do you read the lesson before the class?
answer: Sometimes I do, when I have time.

en: Kindly check my answer sheet once again, sir.
tamil: சார், என் விடைத்தாளை இன்னொரு முறை தயவுசெஞ்சு பாருங்க.
explain: 'Kindly' is a formal and polite word, common in Indian English.
usage: Use it with a lecturer when you think a mark is missing.
leelaQ: How do you ask politely for a second look at something?
answer: I say please check once more, sir.

en: Our college is organising a technical symposium next week.
tamil: எங்க காலேஜ் அடுத்த வாரம் ஒரு டெக்னிக்கல் சிம்போசியம் நடத்துது.
context: Inviting a friend to an event.
explain: 'Is organising' with a future time shows a fixed arrangement.
usage: Use it to invite friends or juniors to a college event.
leelaQ: Do you take part in college events?
answer: Yes, I take part in quiz competitions.

en: I always keep my phone away while studying.
tamil: நான் படிக்கும்போது எப்பவும் என் போனை தள்ளி வச்சிடுவேன்.
explain: 'Always' comes before the main verb. 'While studying' shortens 'while I am studying'.
usage: Use it when you give focus tips to friends or your children.
leelaQ: What distracts you the most when you study?
answer: My phone distracts me the most, so I keep it in another room.

en: How long do you study every day?
tamil: நீ தினமும் எவ்வளவு நேரம் படிப்ப?
explain: 'How long' asks for a length of time. 'Every day' shows habit.
usage: Use it to compare study habits with a friend.
leelaQ: What is a good number of study hours for you?
answer: Four hours a day is good for me.

en: The students are presenting their projects in the hall.
tamil: மாணவர்கள் ஹால்ல தங்களோட ப்ராஜெக்ட்களை சமர்ப்பிச்சிட்டு இருக்காங்க.
context: Telling a visitor what is happening.
explain: 'Are presenting' shows an action in progress. 'Their' belongs to the students.
usage: Use it when you show a guest around a college or a school.
leelaQ: Have you ever presented something in front of a class?
answer: Yes, I once presented my project to the whole class.
